papers.abstract: We interrogated data from 217 subjects with primary myelofibrosis (PMF) diagnosed before 2001 to identify covariates at diagnosis associated with long-term survival. Forty-one survived more than 25 years. Long-term survivors were more often female, younger than 50 years and less likely to have anemia, splenomegaly, increased blood CD34-positive cells, a JAK2V617F variant, and more likely to have grade-0 bone marrow fibrosis and increased platelets. In multivariable logistic regression analyses, age 450 × 10⁹/L, and grade-0 bone marrow fibrosis independently predicted long-term survival. These co-variate associations were confirmed in Cox regression with landmark analyses. Long-term survivors had a lower cumulative incidence of anemia and thrombocytopenia during follow-up. Identifying long-term survivors at diagnosis provides clinically meaningful prognostic information in PMF and may influence therapy decisions.

papers.abstract: Time to surgery (TTS) for breast cancer has been increasing for decades, with delays associated with worse survival. A 2022 Commission on Cancer (CoC) quality measure requires upfront surgery within 60 days after diagnosis (BCSdx). The long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic on TTS and compliance with BCSdx are unknown. Using the National Cancer Database, the study identified 520,967 women with a diagnosis of clinical stages I to III invasive breast cancer from 2014 to 2023 who underwent upfront surgery. Time to surgery was defined as days from diagnosis to definitive surgery. Diagnosis year was modeled continuously and categorically (pre-pandemic 2014-2019, pandemic onset 2020, post-pandemic onset 2021-2023). Linear and logistic regression were used to identify factors associated with TTS and odds of not having surgery in ≤ 60 days. Between 2014 and 2023, the mean TTS increased from 37 to 50 days (+ 13 days). Compared with 2014-2019, the 2021-2023 period was associated with + 7.51 mean days (95% confidence interval [CI], 7.35-7.67 days) and 1.90 times (95% CI, 1.87-1.94 times) increased odds of not meeting BCSdx in the multivariable analysis. Longer TTS also was associated with immediate reconstruction (β = + 8.27 days), uninsured status (β = + 7.99 days), and diagnosis at another facility (β = + 6.55 days). The proportion of patients with a TTS of ≤ 60 days declined from 88% to 74%. The strongest predictors of noncompliance were uninsured status (odds ratio [OR], 2.10), diagnosis at another facility (OR, 1.81), immediate reconstruction (OR, 1.81), black race (OR, 1.72), and Hispanic ethnicity (OR, 1.70). The increase in TTS for breast cancer accelerated after the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, with a concomitant decrease in BCSdx compliance. Strategies to improve care coordination, particularly for at-risk populations, are needed to address this quality measure.

papers.abstract: Adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibition (ICI) for stage IIB/IIC melanoma was approved in December 2021 based on recurrence-free survival benefit without mature overall survival data. Given uncertainty regarding the risk-benefit balance in this population, we evaluated real-world utilization of adjuvant ICI in the first year following FDA approval and compared uptake with historical patterns observed in stage III melanoma. The National Cancer Database (NCDB) and Mayo Clinic Cancer Registry were queried for patients with stage IIB/IIC melanoma diagnosed in 2019-2020 (pre-approval) and 2022 (post-approval). Utilization was compared with historical patterns for stage III melanoma surrounding its December 2017 FDA approval. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with receipt of adjuvant ICI. Among 7039 patients with stage IIB/IIC melanoma in NCDB, adjuvant ICI use increased from 5% pre-approval to 32% post-approval (P < .0001), with higher utilization in stage IIC (40%) than IIB (27%). Younger age was the only consistent patient-level factor associated with treatment. Within our tertiary care system, 21% of eligible patients received adjuvant ICI post-approval. By comparison, stage III utilization at NCDB sites increased from 27 to 58% in the first year following its FDA approval. Adjuvant ICI use for stage IIB/IIC melanoma increased following FDA approval; however, most eligible patients did not receive therapy, and overall utilization remained lower than historical patterns observed for stage III disease, suggesting selective adoption driven by risk-benefit considerations.

papers.abstract: Chronic pain is a major global health burden with a substantial but incompletely understood genetic basis. Although genome-wide association studies have identified multiple common-variant loci for pain-related traits, the contribution of rare coding variants to chronic pain susceptibility, biological mechanisms, and shared architecture across pain phenotypes remains unclear. We performed an exome-wide association study across ten chronic pain phenotypes using whole-exome sequencing data from 327,642 European participants in the UK Biobank. Variant-level and gene-level association analyses were conducted to identify common and rare coding signals. Downstream analyses included conditional analysis, statistical fine-mapping, validation in non-European populations, replication in independent cohorts, cross-trait meta-analysis, colocalization, pathway and tissue enrichment, single-cell enrichment, summary-data-based Mendelian randomization, and estimation of heritability and genetic correlation from common and rare variants. We identified 286 significant variant-level associations arising from 235 unique variants mapped to 117 genes, including 13 novel lead variants and 44 independent lead signals. Gene-level analyses identified ten significant genes driven predominantly by rare functional variants: ADAMTSL5, ANKRD12, ARID5A, DPP7, GMCL1, HCK, KIF20B, SLC13A1, UBR2, and ZNF558. Functional analyses implicated pathways related to nervous system development, axonogenesis, and synaptic organization, with enrichment in brain tissues and hTRPM8-expressing dorsal root ganglion neurons. Mendelian randomization analyses highlighted convergent regulatory effects across neural and immune-related tissues. Heritability analyses showed that rare coding variants explained a modest proportion of variance relative to common variants but exhibited larger average effects in the most damaging functional classes, particularly high-confidence loss-of-function variants. Genetic correlation analyses revealed shared genetic components among chronic pain conditions and positive correlations with selected psychiatric and nervous system disorders. These findings provide a comprehensive map of coding variation underlying chronic pain and show that both common and rare coding variants contribute to its genetic architecture. Rare coding variants explain only a limited fraction of heritability but offer strong mechanistic insight by implicating discrete genes and pathways related to neuronal development, neuroimmune signaling, and tissue homeostasis. This work advances understanding of chronic pain biology and provides a foundation for future multi-ancestry studies and functional validation.

papers.abstract: Young breast cancer (YBC), defined as diagnosis at or before the age of 40 years, is characterized by an aggressive phenotype and poor prognosis. The tumor microenvironment (TME), comprising immune and stromal cells, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression and is closely associated with clinical outcomes. However, alterations in cell states and the organization of multicellular ecosystems within the YBC microenvironment remain poorly understood. We analyzed 7379 bulk transcriptome samples and spatial transcriptomic data from eight samples using EcoTyper and complementary spatial analyses. The abundance of CD4+ T cells (S07), fibroblasts (S05), monocytes/macrophages (S09), and epithelial cells (S05) was significantly lower in young than in older patients with breast cancer. CD4+ T cells (S07), fibroblasts (S05), and monocytes/macrophages (S09) formed a spatially organized multicellular ecosystem with putative interactions involving CDH1-PTPRF/ERBB3. Lower ecosystem abundance was associated with poorer prognosis, including among patients who did not achieve a pathological complete response after neoadjuvant therapy. These findings identify a distinct multicellular ecosystem within the YBC microenvironment, providing insights into the microenvironmental features associated with disease progression.

papers.abstract: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) enables gentle, rapid and efficient volumetric imaging of biological specimens. Despite its potential, LSFM has fragmented into multiple variants, each narrowly optimized for specific samples or imaging regimes, limiting its broad applicability. Here we introduce the multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM), an adaptable LSFM platform for high-resolution imaging ranging from subcellular dynamics to whole organisms and cleared tissues. miOPM supports seamless interchangeability of oil, water and air objectives and maintains diffraction-limited performance across a refractive index range of 1.33 to 1.51. It is compatible with standard sample mounting, current clearing protocols and high-throughput 3D imaging. We leverage miOPM to image diverse biological specimens at multiple spatial scales. By expanding the adaptability and ease of use of LSFM, miOPM is poised to democratize advanced 3D imaging.

papers.abstract: H2AK119ub (H2Aub) and H3K27me3, which are deposited by the Polycomb group (PcG) complexes PRC1 and PRC2, respectively, cooperatively repress developmental genes. However, in human preimplantation embryos, H3K27me3 undergoes genome-wide erasure and subsequent restoration. How H3K27me3 is reestablished and whether PcG complexes still regulate gene repression in human embryos remain unknown. Here, we profiled H2Aub dynamics from human gametes to blastocysts. H2Aub emerges in GC-rich regions as early as the two-cell stage, progressively accumulates at both active and inactive genes, and further culminates at PcG targets in later stages. H3K27me3 is weakly correlated with H2Aub in oocytes and two-cell embryos but colocalizes with H2Aub at H3K4me3-depleted, inactive PcG targets in blastocysts. Loss of H2Aub abolishes H3K27me3 reestablishment at PcG targets causing moderate derepression, accompanied by ectopic H3K27me3 deposition and impaired embryonic development. Finally, H2Aub and DNA methylation cooperatively maintain H3K27me3 patterning in human embryonic stem cells. Therefore, H2Aub-dependent H3K27me3 deposition underlies the earliest establishment of Polycomb repression in humans.

papers.abstract: Human societies are drawing on wild species for food, fuel, medicines, and recreation. Yet, it remains unclear whether different types of human use target species with common or unique ecological roles. Here we show that humans use a fourth (26%) of the freshwater fish species and these species occupy almost half (45.2%) of the global spectrum of fish morphological diversity. Yet, used species harbour unique trait combinations, that differ according to the way humans use the species such as fisheries, aquaculture, game fish and aquarium. Moreover, the species targeted by humans are characterised by traits that are predominantly associated with threatened species. By simulating the extinction of threatened species used by humans, we revealed a pronounced and non-random erosion of the morphological spectrum. Understanding the trait-based impacts of human use is thus essential to buffer human impact on natural resources. Conservation should therefore safeguard threatened species but also preserve irreplaceable trait combinations that support unique ecological strategies.

papers.abstract: Global glacier models typically rely on temperature-index mass balance calculations forced with aggregated meteorological data, limiting their ability to resolve short-term variability. Here, we develop a daily-resolution version of the Global Glacier Evolution Model (GloGEM), which we apply globally and compare against the monthly configuration. Our results show that the daily model more closely reproduces mass balance observations and provides a more detailed representation of glacier runoff. Accounting for short-term meteorological variability leads to systematically greater projected mass loss, with up to 25% greater loss in Svalbard. These differences arise from extreme melt days, precipitation-phase transitions, and surface-type feedbacks not fully represented at monthly resolution. Globally, the daily model yields ice volume losses of 26 ± 10% under low-emission and 47 ± 17% under high-emission scenarios over 2025-2100 (ensemble mean ± 1 StD), resulting in an additional 5-10% mass loss (20-33 mm of global mean sea-level rise) relative to the monthly implementation. Resolving high-frequency forcing, or accounting for its effects through parameterisations, is therefore essential for robust glacier projections, while its omission may systematically underestimate future glacier loss.

papers.abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron-hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron-phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron-phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

papers.abstract: Retinoic acid-inducible gene-I (RIG-I) plays a pivotal role in recognizing and combating RNA viruses in humans, and it has become a drug target of significant interest. RIG-I agonists composed of dsRNA represent antiviral and antitumor therapies, however the development of small-molecule RIG-I agonists, with their potential for improved pharmacokinetics, remains an unmet need. Here, we report small-molecule RIG-I agonists that directly activate the RIG-I receptor protein. These agonists stimulate the first step in RIG-I signaling by triggering release of the signaling domains (CARDs) from an autorepressed form of the protein. This was achieved by developing a sensitive high-throughput screening (HTS) assay that directly monitors CARD expulsion through optical methods. The resulting screen hits were refined and optimized, leading to a specific RIG-I agonist that induces a robust interferon response. This study establishes a pharmacophore and assay for development of small molecules that precisely modulate RIG-I signaling.

papers.abstract: Periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a devastating complication of total joint arthroplasty, mainly caused by bacterial biofilm formation and antibiotic resistance. Traditional static surfaces rely on contact killing-based bactericidal properties and cannot reliably clear mature biofilms. In this study, we fabricate a remote-activated dynamic biomimetic system, namely a movable magnetic topographic surface (MMTS). Here we show that under the exposure of external electromagnetic field (EMF), the anchored Janus nano-heterodimers oscillate periodically to mechanically disrupt bacterial membranes and eradicates biofilms of Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli. This mechanical force can also activates Piezo1 mechanosensitive ion channel in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs), inducing calcium oscillations, upregulating gene expression of Runx2 and BMP2, and enhancing extracellular matrix mineralization. In vivo, MMTS combined with EMF exposure eliminates local infection and promoted osseointegration. This remote-activated dynamic biomimetic strategy offers a promising multifunctional platform for PJI treatment, and improved implant osteointegration in clinical orthopedics.

papers.abstract: Endocytosis regulates receptor trafficking and signaling, yet its role in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains unclear. We analyzed transcriptomic data from 15,025 CRC tumors to evaluate gene expression in clathrin-mediated endocytosis (CME) and the endosomal sorting complexes required for transport (ESCRT) pathway. Pathway-level signatures were compared across consensus molecular subtypes (CMS) and examined in relation to oncogenic signaling programs, while individual endocytosis-related genes were evaluated for associations with clinical outcomes in an independent randomized trial cohort. Expression of CME and ESCRT pathways varied by CMS, with the highest expression in CMS4 and the lowest in CMS3. Endocytosis signatures correlated with multiple oncogenic signaling pathways, including MAPK, TGF-β, WNT, PI3K, NOTCH, and angiogenesis, suggesting broad links between endocytic activity and tumor biology. In the randomized phase III CALGB/SWOG 80405 trial, low expression of AP2M1-a core adaptor in the CME complex-was significantly associated with longer overall survival and progression-free survival in patients treated with anti-EGFR agents, but not in those receiving anti-VEGF agents. These findings suggest that endocytic trafficking may be associated with oncogenic signaling and differential therapeutic benefit in patients with metastatic CRC. The endocytosis pathway reflects biologically relevant heterogeneity in CRC and may help guide therapeutic stratification.

papers.abstract: Eukaryotic cells contain various membrane- and non-membrane-bound organelles, whose spatial and functional organization underpins intracellular homeostasis. Organelle coordination is governed by complex signaling and metabolic networks, often facilitated by direct physical contacts and molecular exchange. Mitochondria, as central hubs of bioenergetic and metabolic activity, are essential to functional coordination among cellular organelles. They engage in diverse cellular processes, encompassing ATP production, biosynthesis of key metabolites, calcium ion buffering, redox balance, and cellular turnover. To preserve their integrity and functionality, dysfunctional mitochondria undergo selective elimination via mitophagy, a specialized form of macroautophagy. Mitophagy plays dual roles in maintaining mitochondrial fidelity and actively shapes interorganelle communication. Through bidirectional signaling, mitophagy influences the activity of multiple organelles, including the endoplasmic reticulum, nucleus, lysosomes, peroxisomes, and lipid droplets. This interorganelle crosstalk is essential for adapting to metabolic stress, maintaining redox balance, and coordinating cell fate decisions. In this review, we explore the intricate signaling networks connecting mitophagy with various organelles and discuss how these interactions influence organ function and overall cellular health. We also highlight emerging small-molecule modulators of mitophagy, providing insight into potential therapeutic strategies aimed at restoring or enhancing organelle communication in pathological conditions.

papers.abstract: Regulated cell death (RCD) is characterized by distinct molecular execution mechanisms, but its initiation, progression, and biological consequences are increasingly recognized as being shaped by cellular metabolism. Bioenergetic state, redox homeostasis, nutrient availability, metal ion metabolism, inflammatory metabolism, and organelle function collectively determine cellular susceptibility to death and influence the activation and execution of diverse RCD programs. In this review, we synthesize the metabolic hallmarks of established, independently validated, and recently proposed forms of RCD, highlighting both their mechanistic diversity and their extensive metabolic convergence. We then examine the endogenous mechanisms that maintain metabolic homeostasis and discuss how their disruption reshapes cell death responses in human disease and therapeutic contexts. Together, these insights provide a guide to the metabolic landscape of RCD and reveal metabolism not only as a modifier of cell death, but as a fundamental determinant of when, how, and with what consequences cells die. We conclude by discussing key conceptual and mechanistic challenges and emerging opportunities for therapeutically exploiting the metabolic control of RCD.

papers.abstract: Short-wave infrared (SWIR) emitters underpin applications in communication, imaging and sensing, yet efficient, scalable devices remain limited. Colloidal InAs quantum dots (InAs CQDs) offer a compelling, cost-effective alternative to conventional epitaxial SWIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs). However, developing heavy-metal-free InAs CQDs for emission beyond 1400 nm is hindered by lattice mismatch during core/shell growth, which degrades photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). Furthermore, integrating CQDs into LEDs often introduces severe interfacial quenching and intrinsic charge imbalances. Here we report a highly efficient heavy-metal-free SWIR LED operating at 1525 nm, enabled by tailored injection strategies and oxidation-induced interfacial engineering. Optimized high-temperature ZnCl₂ treatment and continuous precursor injection improve shell nucleation and growth, while controlled interfacial oxidation is associated with reduced shell-thickness-dependent strain signatures and improved PLQY retention during shell thickening. Together, these strategies yield measured PLQYs exceeding 55% for emission beyond 1400 nm. Moreover, we demonstrate that incorporating a semiconducting InAs CQD interlayer effectively suppresses interfacial quenching and regulates electron over-injection. Combined with a doped hole-transport layer to reduce series resistance, our optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 3.5% and a record radiance of ~17 W sr-1 m-2, alongside a T50 operational lifetime of 16 h. Our findings suggest that integrating mechanism-driven shell growth with rational device engineering offers a strategy to overcome current bottlenecks in colloidal emitters, facilitating the transition toward short-wave infrared applications.

papers.abstract: Individual variation in human attractiveness to mosquitoes critically influences vector-borne disease transmission, and this phenomenon arises from multiple underlying factors. This study integrated human skin microbiome profiling, non-human primate in situ intervention, and volatilomics to uncover a microbial-mediated mechanism underlying host-specific mosquito repellency. Bacillus species were identified as a microbial signature associated with reduced mosquito attraction in humans. Targeted Intervention of B. licheniformis and B. paralicheniformis on primate skin was sufficient to significantly reduce mosquito attraction, thereby establishing a causal microbial contribution beyond descriptive correlations. Mechanistic analyses revealed that Bacillus enrichment reprogrammed the skin volatilome, specifically increasing the abundance of aromatic and fatty acid-derived effectors, such as p-Cresol and decanoic acid, which are associated with repellency phenotypes. Together, these findings revealed a potential role of skin commensals in shaping mosquito host-seeking behavior, providing a molecular basis for microbiome-informed and bio-inspired strategies for mosquito disease control.

papers.abstract: Differentiating true progression (TP) from pseudoprogression (PsP) after chemoradiation for glioblastoma remains clinically difficult. We evaluated externally validated diagnostic performance of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based machine learning models and appraised study quality and transparency. PubMed, Embase, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library were searched through October 1, 2025 (PROSPERO registration CRD420251144894). Eligible adult glioblastoma studies used MRI-based machine learning to distinguish TP from PsP against histopathology and/or clinicoradiologic follow-up. The primary meta-analysis included external test cohorts with extractable 2 × 2 data; internal and combined internal and external test analyses were secondary. Diagnostic accuracy was synthesized with bivariate random-effects models. Thirty-one studies including 2,344 patients undergoing imaging assessment were included. Seven external test cohorts, including 219 patient observations, entered the primary meta-analysis. Pooled sensitivity was 0.78 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.63-0.88), specificity was 0.75 (95% CI, 0.63-0.84), and summary area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was 0.81 (bootstrap 95% CI, 0.69-0.91). Internal test cohorts showed higher apparent performance than external cohorts (AUC, 0.91 vs 0.81), but the difference was not statistically significant (difference, -0.09; 95% CI, -0.22 to 0.02; P = 0.12). Risk of bias was frequently high or unclear, and reporting transparency was heterogeneous. MRI-based machine learning showed moderate-to-good external validation performance for TP-versus-PsP discrimination, but evidence remains limited by small external test cohorts, bias, and incomplete reporting. Larger transparent multicenter validations are needed before routine clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Postoperative delirium is a common and serious complication in older surgical patients and has been associated with increased morbidity, healthcare costs, long-term functional decline and mortality. To determine whether postoperative delirium is associated with functional status, quality of life, institutionalisation and mortality at 1 year after surgery in a large multicentre surgical cohort. Prospective multicentre observational study. Forty-three hospitals in Spain. Surgical patients were recruited in November 2023 and assessed for delirium 48 h after surgery, with follow-up at 1 year. A total of 2442 adult surgical patients undergoing elective or urgent procedures requiring hospital admission. Postoperative delirium was assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method (CAM), CAM for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the telephone-administered 4AT according to clinical setting. None. Functional status and quality of life at 1 year assessed using the 12-item World Health Organization Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS 2.0). Secondary outcomes included institutionalisation and mortality. After excluding 81 deaths and 462 nonresponders, the 1-year telephone follow-up was completed for 1899 patients. Postoperative delirium within the first 48 h was independently associated with a 4.6-point higher WHODAS score at 1 year: adjusted mean difference = 4.60 [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.57 to 7.64, P = 0.003]. Delirium was also associated with increased institutionalisation and higher mortality: odds ratio (OR) 2.5 (95% CI, 1.07 to 5.84, P = 0.03), and (16.7 vs. 3.1%; P < 0.001), including 30-day, 60-day, and 365-day mortality (all P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative delirium is independently associated with long-term functional decline, loss of independence, institutionalisation and increased 1-year mortality. These findings highlight delirium as a key perioperative complication and support prevention strategies and structured long-term follow-up after surgery. ClinicalTrials.gov (identifier: NC-T06127901).

papers.abstract: The lack of tumor-specific targeting by oncolytic viruses (OVs) restricts their therapeutic potential. Here, we report a "cap-linker" strategy to modify the vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV) glycoprotein (G protein, VSV-GIN). The modified VSV (Pro-VSVIN) loses its ability to infect cells until present in the tumor microenvironment, where the linker is cleaved by tumor-enriched matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs). When Pro-VSVIN is armed with a single-chain IL-12 (Pro-VSVIN-IL-12) and systemically injected into MC38 tumor-bearing mice, Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 eradicates established tumors while avoiding systemic toxicity, and elicits long-term anti-tumor immune memory. Systemic administration of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 also markedly inhibits the growth of metastatic cancers in the lung. The efficacy of Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 was further improved when combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade. Compared to WT VSVIN that carries IL-12, intravenously injected Pro-VSVIN-IL-12 leads to strong Th1 immunity, near abolishment of regulatory T cells, and potent CD8+ T cell activation and clonal expansion in tumors. This preclinical work demonstrates a new tumor-specific targeting strategy of VSV for enhanced immunotherapy safety with superior efficacy.

papers.abstract: This educational review describes the historical development of pediatric congenital cardiac anesthesia and its expanding role in the care of patients with congenital heart disease (CHD). Over the past eight decades, the specialty has evolved from an era in which few congenital heart defects were surgically treatable and perioperative mortality was high to one in which survival into adulthood is expected for most children with CHD. This transformation has been driven by parallel advances in surgical techniques, cardiopulmonary bypass technology, myocardial protection, monitoring, intensive care, and anesthetic management. From the first successful patent ductus arteriosus ligation in 1938 to the development of fetal cardiac interventions and the many major technological and scientific advances of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, anesthesiologists have played a pivotal role in improving the care of patients with CHD. As survival has improved, the population of adults and elderly patients living with repaired or palliated CHD has grown, and the specialty's focus has expanded beyond reducing perioperative mortality to improving lifelong outcomes. Today, congenital cardiac anesthesiologists are integral members of multidisciplinary teams responsible for perioperative risk assessment, hemodynamic optimization, neuroprotection, coagulation management, mechanical circulatory support, and enhanced recovery. The history of the specialty highlights the importance of multidisciplinary collaboration and continued scientific progress in improving patient safety, recovery, and long-term outcomes.

papers.abstract: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and chronic kidney disease face persistent risks despite standard care. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide lacks real-world renoprotective evidence in high-risk Chinese populations relative to non-incretin-based standard care. This multicenter, ambispective cohort study enrolled 3305 patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, renal impairment, and elevated cardiovascular risk at six Chinese tertiary institutions (median follow-up 36.4 months; trial registration: ChiCTR2300073001). Data were extracted via an artificial intelligence-enhanced pipeline. Co-primary analyzes comprised multivariable-adjusted Cox regression and 1:1 propensity score matching (332 per group); pre-specified landmark analyzes at 6 and 12 months addressed immortal time bias. Polyethylene glycol-loxenatide was associated with a reduced risk of the primary kidney composite outcome in the original cohort (hazard ratio [HR], 0.49; 95% CI, 0.25-0.95; P = 0.035), which was corroborated in the propensity score matched cohort (HR, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.20-0.97; P = 0.043) and progressive across 6-month (HR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.19-0.84) and 12-month (HR, 0.33; 95% CI, 0.14-0.75) landmarks. While a reduction in 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events was observed in the unmatched cohort (HR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.43-0.85; P = 0.004), this association was not sustained in the matched analysis (HR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.57-1.48; P = 0.735). In conclusion, long-term therapy was associated with an attenuated risk of major renal events. Given the null findings in the matched cohort, the cardiovascular observations are exploratory and require randomized confirmation.

papers.abstract: Women anesthesiologists face unique challenges that threaten their well-being and retention. This includes high rates of imposter phenomenon, higher rates of attrition compared to male colleagues, and high rates of suicide. While group coaching is increasingly recognized as a developmental modality to foster growth in complex work environments, gaps remain in understanding how group coaching supports women who face imposter syndrome or how effective this modality is for women anesthesiologists. This study examines the impact of a pilot group coaching intervention that focused on addressing imposter syndrome in women anesthesiologists participating in the Women's Empowerment and Leadership Initiative (WELI). Fifteen women pediatric anesthesiologists, split across two groups, took part in seven monthly group coaching sessions. A post-coaching survey was then conducted in which participants were asked about their experiences before and after group coaching. Eight of the participants volunteered to participate in semi-structured interviews about their experiences. Qualitative data were coded using an inductive thematic analysis approach. The survey showed that following group coaching, participants demonstrated an increase in self-reported compassion and acceptance of others. They also reported learning more about themselves and how to amend their own behavior in helpful ways compared to pre-intervention. Two overarching themes emerged: a sense of community (fueled by psychological safety, validation, shared experience, and addressing imposter syndrome through the group coaching) and tools gained (including clearer priorities, work/life integration, and proactive social support). Results of this pilot intervention suggest group coaching programs for anesthesiologists have the potential to build resilience in the current work environment, thereby benefiting not only individuals but the anesthesiology workforce as a whole.

papers.abstract: The addition of entinostat, a histone deacetylase inhibitor, to exemestane has demonstrated improved progression-free survival (PFS) in hormone receptor-positive (HR + ), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) advanced breast cancer (ABC) following endocrine therapy failure in the EOC103A3101 randomized trial (NCT03538171). This study reports long-term overall survival (OS) results. In this study, 354 patients with HR + /HER2- ABC that had recurred or progressed after endocrine therapy were randomized (2:1) to receive entinostat plus exemestane (n = 235) or placebo plus exemestane (n = 119). After a median follow-up of 31.8 months, the median OS was 38.6 months (95% confidence interval [CI]: 29.6-44.0) in the entinostat-exemestane group versus 29.2 months (95% CI: 22.5-41.6) in the placebo-exemestane group (hazard ratio [HR] 0.83, 95% CI: 0.62-1.10, P = 0.184). The entinostat-exemestane group demonstrated more pronounced OS benefits when adjusting subsequent antitumor therapies such as cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors, or the combination of endocrine therapy, CDK4/6 inhibitors, and chemotherapy. The sensitivity analysis based on the per-protocol set showed more significant OS benefits. The median time to post-discontinuation chemotherapy and chemotherapy-free survival in the entinostat-exemestane group were 11.7 and 9.3 months, respectively, compared to 6.8 and 5.6 months in the placebo-exemestane group (both P < 0.05). Grade ≥3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 65.5% of patients in the entinostat-exemestane group, without new safety signals observed. In conclusion, among patients with HR + /HER2- ABC after endocrine therapy failure, entinostat plus exemestane was associated with a numerically longer OS, with an acceptable safety profile.

papers.abstract: Quadruplet therapy, combining anti-CD38 antibodies, immunomodulatory drugs, proteasome inhibitors and dexamethasone, is now the standard induction treatment for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (NDMM). However, treatment response is heterogeneous and molecular predictors are needed to guide early therapeutic decisions. We performed integrated genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of 423 tumor samples from patients with NDMM from the MIDAS cohort to characterize molecular heterogeneity and its association with measurable residual disease (MRD) after quadruplet induction with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Isa-KRd). Postinduction MRD-negativity rates varied significantly across gene expression subtypes, with HP1/HP3 and MS groups showing superior responses compared to the MF and CD2 subtypes. B cell differentiation was associated with MRD positivity, while proliferation and MYC programs were associated with MRD negativity. These MRD-associated transcriptomic features were independently validated in the CASSIOPEIA cohort. Whole-genome sequencing revealed both known (APOBEC mutagenesis, chromothripsis) and new genomic instability phenotypes validated in the MMRF cohort. New driver alterations were identified with independent validation across three external cohorts with multiple myeloma (MMRF, MANHATTAN and CASSIOPEIA; 1,451 cases). Genomic instability features and driver genes such as CCND1 and MYC correlated with differential MRD outcomes. DNA methylation profiling identified nine MRD-linked subgroups distinguished by the extent of hypomethylation in quiescent chromatin and cis/trans signatures of driver translocations. A multimodal random forest model integrating genomic, transcriptomic and epigenomic features predicted MRD status after induction, with an area under the curve of 0.77, outperforming clinical and genomic models, while providing comparable discrimination and improved calibration relative to the transcriptomic and epigenomic models. These findings define a multiomic classification of NDMM linked to Isa-KRd response. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04934475 .

papers.abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442.

papers.abstract: Accurate positioning of central venous catheter (CVC) tips is essential to avoid complications, yet consistent appropriate placement within the superior vena cava remains challenging without a simple method for depth adjustment. To develop and temporally validate a simple computed tomography-based (CT-based) body surface landmark approach for estimating optimal insertion depth (OID) and to assess its impact on appropriate catheter tip positioning. Single-centre prospective observational cohort study. Tertiary care hospital in Japan; February 2017 to June 2019. Adult patients undergoing surgery requiring CVC placement via the right internal jugular vein with preoperative chest CT. After exclusions, 86 patients were included in the derivation cohort and 100 in the validation cohort. In the derivation cohort, insertion depth was determined by the attending anaesthesiologist; in the validation cohort, it was determined using a model derived from the derivation cohort. The primary outcome was the proportion of appropriately placed catheter tips. The final model retained the insertion point-to-body surface landmark distance (ILD), defined using a body surface landmark corresponding to the CT-identified midpoint of Zone B, as the sole predictor: OID (cm) = 0.64 × ILD + 3.64. The proportion of appropriately placed catheter tips was higher in the validation cohort than in the derivation cohort (92.0% (95% CI, 85.0 to 95.9%) vs. 73.3% (95% CI, 63.1 to 81.5%); P < 0.001). Model-guided placement was associated with increased likelihood of appropriate positioning (adjusted odds ratio 4.68 (95% CI, 1.97 to 12.27)). papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) exhibit remarkable functional heterogeneity, with conserved subtypes observed across diverse malignancies. However, their shared roles in shaping the tumor microenvironment (TME) and their dynamic plasticity remain incompletely understood. In this study, through integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic profiling across four cancer types, we identified two distinct immunomodulatory CAF states, termed antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) and matrix-producing CAFs (mCAFs). Across multiple solid tumors, apCAFs were associated with enhanced anti-tumor immune features and favorable prognosis, whereas mCAFs were associated with immunosuppressive characteristics and poorer clinical outcomes. Spatial analyses revealed distinct localization patterns of apCAFs and mCAFs within the TME. Functionally, patient-derived apCAFs promoted T-cell migration, proliferation, and activation, whereas mCAFs suppressed these responses in vitro. Pan-cancer analyses further revealed a strong inverse correlation between apCAF and mCAF abundance across tumor tissues. Mechanistically, IFN-γ and TGF-β-associated signaling contexts were linked to distinct CAF transcriptional programs, with IFN-γ promoting apCAF-associated features and TGF-β favoring mCAF-associated features, suggesting a potential role of cytokine context in shaping CAF state heterogeneity. Clinically, apCAFs correlated with favorable immunotherapy response, whereas mCAFs predicted poor therapeutic outcomes. Collectively, these findings identify conserved immunomodulatory CAF subtypes across cancers, reveal distinct cytokine-associated CAF programs, and support stromal reprogramming as a promising strategy to enhance immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract: New-onset diabetes (NOD) potentially associated with pancreatic cancer (PC) requires further investigation to assess its potential as a tool for PC screening. In this longitudinal nationwide register study, which includes 14,712 PC patients and 18 years of follow-up time (2000-2018), we aimed to assess the prevalence of diabetes by using a large national registry. Survival was analyzed according to diabetes status and duration (long-term diabetes, i.e., DM diagnosed > 3 years prior to PC, NOD, i.e., DM diagnosed 0-3 years prior to PC, or DM diagnosed after PC diagnosis) and treatment status (curative intent vs. palliative) using multivariable Cox regression analysis. Overall, 18% of PC patients had diabetes. The median time interval between DM and PC diagnoses was 4.8 months. In the multivariable Cox regression analysis, only DM diagnosed after PC was associated with worse survival, both in the palliative intent treatment group (HR 1.12, 95% CI 1.03-1.23, p = 0.011) and in the curative intent treatment group (HR 1.44, 95% CI 1.14-1.81, p = 0.002). Among patients diagnosed with diabetes prior to PC, neither long-term nor NOD significantly affected survival. Most of the diabetic PC-patients have been diagnosed with DM within a close proximity of cancer diagnosis. The progression from diabetes to clinically detectable cancer seems to be rapid-less than 6 months. Given the aggressive nature of PC and the fact that NOD can be an early sign, screening may need to begin at the time of diabetes diagnosis. The fact that a DM diagnosis made after a PC diagnosis is associated with worse survival may suggest that pancreatic tumors that cause hyperglycemia are particularly aggressive.

papers.abstract: Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) frequently occur during combination immune checkpoint inhibition. However, their prognostic impact may vary according to organ involvement and severity. In this study, we exploratorily evaluated whether severe non-endocrine irAEs represent a temporally distinct and prognostically unfavorable clinical phenotype in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab. We analyzed 63 patients with mRCC treated with ipilimumab plus nivolumab who were followed for at least 5 years. Patients were categorized into non-irAE, non-severe + severe endocrine irAE, and severe non-endocrine irAE groups. Overall survival (OS) was assessed. Multistate modeling was used to evaluate the transitions between treatment, irAE occurrence, and death. Landmark analyses were performed at 8 and 12 weeks to address immortal time bias. The severe non-endocrine irAE group was associated with inferior OS. The multistate analysis revealed a potentially increased risk of direct transition from ipilimumab plus nivolumab to death in the severe non-endocrine irAE group. A significantly higher proportion of patients in the severe non-endocrine irAE group experienced irAEs within 30 days. No significant association was observed in the 8- and 12-week landmark analyses. In this exploratory retrospective study, severe non-endocrine irAEs showed an association with early onset and potentially unfavorable clinical outcomes in patients with mRCC receiving ipilimumab plus nivolumab. Given the limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation in larger independent cohorts.

papers.abstract: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer worldwide, categorized into melanoma and non-melanoma types. While genetics play a crucial role in the development of skin cancer, recent developments in metabolomics have revealed that circulating metabolites influence genetic risk profiles. In this study, we utilized a bidirectional two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) approach, analyzing metabolite datasets from the Canadian Longitudinal Study of Aging (CLSA) and skin cancer datasets from the UK Biobank. Replication analyses were performed with the 10th round of the FinnGen project. Instrumental variables (IVs) were chosen according to established MR criteria and assessed through the Wald ratio, IVW, MR-Egger, and weighted median methods. Various sensitivity analyses were conducted utilizing Cochrane's Q, Egger's intercept, MR-PRESSO, and leave-one-out (LOO) techniques. After meticulous analysis, we identified causal relationships between circulating metabolites and skin cancer risks. Specifically, levels of 1,2-dilinoleoyl-GPE (18:2/18:2), 1-palmitoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (16:0/18:2), 1-stearoyl-2-arachidonoyl-gpc (18:0/20:4), 1-stearoyl-2-linoleoyl-gpc (18:0/18:2), and Docosapentaenoate n3 DPA, the ratio of Arachidonate (20:4n6) to oleate to vaccenate (18:1), and Oleoyl-linoleoyl-glycerol (18:1 to 18:2) to linoleoyl-arachidonoyl-glycerol (18:2 to 20:4) were linked to non-melanoma skin cancer, whereas levels of trans-urocanate were causally linked to melanoma of skin, and S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) showed a putative association. It should be noted that docosapentaenoate n3 DPA and SAH were each supported by a single SNP and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive causal evidence. Reverse MR analysis highlighted robust causal relationships with 18 and 10 metabolites and non-melanoma skin cancer and melanoma of skin, respectively. These findings enhance our understanding of skin cancer etiology and risk factors, providing genetic evidence for hypothesis-generating associations that support the development of targeted therapies and aid in the identification of potential biomarkers.

papers.abstract: Relapsed or refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B-ALL) patients exhibit heterogeneous responses to CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy. However, current studies primarily focus on the CAR-T cells or the leukemia blasts, and the patient's intrinsic molecular characteristics before treatment remain poorly understood. Fifteen R/R B-ALL patients enrolled in a phase II, single-arm clinical trial (NCT04684147) were stratified at a three-month landmark into 8 good responders and 7 poor responders. Clinical characteristics, genetic alterations and pre-treatment bone marrow transcriptomics were compared between groups, and an exploratory gene-expression score was derived. Differential expression and enrichment analyses identified a myeloid-like signature and upregulation of myeloid-related genes in poor responders. Seven myeloid-related genes were examined in independent patient cohorts, in B-ALL cell lines and at single-cell resolution in one patient; three were expressed by the leukemic cells themselves and four predominantly by monocytes and macrophages. A separate, variance-derived seven-gene least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) score separated response groups in the discovery cohort (apparent area under the curve, AUC 1.00), with bias-corrected and external estimates of approximately 0.57-0.59 (external cohort AUC 0.592, 95% confidence interval 0.356-0.828). Pre-treatment transcriptomic profiling revealed a myeloid-like signature in R/R B-ALL patients with poor CD19 CAR-T response, warranting further investigation as a candidate correlate of treatment outcome.

papers.abstract: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) comprise a group of lethal malignancies, yet developing SCC-specific therapies remains challenging, largely due to a lack of druggable targets. We identify SOX2 condensation as a shared cancer hallmark across esophageal, head and neck, and lung SCCs. Within SOX2, the activation domain 1 (AD1) acts as the condensate-promoting region via its aromatic and hydrophobic residues. Site-specific mutagenesis, orthotopic mouse models, and multi-omics sequencing demonstrate that SOX2 condensates upregulate oncogene expression by enhancing SOX2 chromatin occupancy, H3K27ac enrichment, and chromatin interactions at oncogenic loci such as FGFR2, thereby promoting SCC progression. An FDA-approved drug screen reveals that the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner. Upon ixazomib treatment, the substrate-binding domain of HSP70 blocks SOX2 AD1, selectively dissolving SOX2 condensates, downregulating oncogene expression, and suppressing condensate-positive SCC patient-derived xenografts. These findings highlight targeting SOX2 condensates with proteasome inhibitors as an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. We trace the origin of isoUDCA to a bacterial consortium, which is selectively enriched by estrogen through shaping a specialized intestinal microenvironment. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

papers.abstract: Red-meat-containing diets are epidemiologically associated with diseases of chronic inflammation, while diets that restrict red meat improve health. Yet, it is uncertain how red meat incites inflammation. Here, we discover that ʟ-carnitine, an amino acid highly concentrated in skeletal muscle myocytes, drives inflammasome activation in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-challenged mice and LPS-primed murine and human macrophages. We find that extracellular ʟ-carnitine represses mevalonate synthesis, thereby triggering activation of the pyrin inflammasome, downstream of cellular import by the high-affinity ʟ-carnitine transporter OCTN2. We find that the inflammatory response to skeletal muscle injury also requires pyrin and OCTN2. Thus, in summary, we identify macrophages as sentinels of exogenous and endogenous extracellular ʟ-carnitine that serve as a proxy for skeletal myocyte damage, and we open the field to examine the mechanistic basis for how excess dietary intake of carnitine-rich food drives inflammatory disease.

papers.abstract: Revealing how distributed cortical circuits coordinate behavior in freely moving animals remains a central challenge in systems neuroscience, constrained by limited fields of view, low throughput, and the tethering required by current miniaturized microscopes1-4. Here, we present Airscope, a wireless mesoscope delivering 4 μm lateral resolution across a 6 mm field of view at 12.5 Hz, weighing 1.0 gram. An aspheric-lens design achieves a 2.84× shorter total track length than previous miniaturized microscopes1,2,5,6 while matching the neuron yield of benchtop one-photon mesoscopes; a tailored wireless link supports cable-free calcium imaging from >8,500 neurons per animal (25‑fold increase). Paired with a zero-shot behavior analyzer, Airscope enables cortical imaging across rich behavioral conditions, including room-scale enriched arenas, swimming assays, and multi-organ implantation, with concurrent recording from multiple animals. Using Airscope, we demonstrate versatile applications of untethered cortical imaging across diverse behavioral paradigms. We identify cortical activity patterns across multiple dorsal regions that correlate with behavioral signatures of social dominance, and show dorsal-cortical population activity prospectively decodes competition outcomes across paired animals. We observe reward-location-associated cortical activity patterns during maze exploration, and characterize Granger-causal influence from spinal cord to cortex during fear conditioning, enabled by simultaneous brain-spinal recordings. By uniting large-scale, cellular-resolution recording with unconstrained behavior, Airscope makes naturalistic, multi-animal cortical recording experimentally practical, and provides a broadly accessible technology for systems neuroscience.

papers.abstract: To identify preoperative predictors of postoperative renal replacement therapy (RRT) in patients undergoing left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation to help guide interventions that could decrease the incidence of new dialysis-dependent acute kidney injury (AKI). Retrospective cohort study. A single-center, university hospital. There were 159 adult patients undergoing LVAD implantation between July 2012 to July 2024 INTERVENTIONS: Retrospective analysis of preoperative variables, including hemoglobin, creatinine, MELD score, and intraoperative RBC transfusion volume and their effect on the primary outcome of new dialysis-dependent AKI. New dialysis-dependent AKI occurred in 17% of patients. Preoperative hemoglobin was inversely associated with RRT risk; every 1-g/dL increase was associated with a 21% reduction in odds ratio (OR 0.79; CI 0.65-0.97, p = .023). Intraoperative red blood cell transfusion volume was a major predictor, with patients receiving 0 to 5 units having significantly lower OR than those receiving ≥11 units (OR 0.01; 95% CI 0.001-0.11; p < .001). MELD scores between 10 and 20 also increased the OR (OR 3.10; 95% CI 1.07-9.00; p = .038). Additionally, needing new dialysis was strongly associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation (OR 8.76; 95% CI 2.52-30.5; p = .001) and postoperative gastrointestinal bleeding (OR 3.73; 95% CI 1.48-9.40; p = .005). Preoperative hemoglobin and perioperative red blood cell transfusion volume are significant and potentially actionable, modifiable risk factors for postoperative RRT in LVAD recipients. Optimizing preoperative hemoglobin may offer a targeted strategy to reduce RRT rates in this high-risk population.

papers.abstract: PD-L1-mediated immunosuppression is a key mechanism underlying tumor immune evasion, whereas PD-1/PD-L1 blockade therapies remain limited by low response rates and acquired resistance. Through small-molecule screening, we identify isobavachalcone (IBC), a naturally derived compound that modulates PD-L1 homeostasis by targeting the deubiquitinase OTUB1. Mechanistically, IBC targets OTUB1 at the His217 residue and suppresses its deubiquitinase activity, thereby promoting K48-linked polyubiquitination of PD-L1 and its proteasome-dependent degradation. Functionally, IBC reduces tumor cell PD-L1 expression and enhances CD8+ T cell-mediated cytotoxicity. In PD-L1-deficient tumor models, IBC fails to further enhance antitumor activity, indicating that PD-L1 is required for IBC-mediated immune regulation. Moreover, IBC combined with anti-CTLA-4 therapy further enhanced antitumor efficacy. Together, these findings highlight IBC as a potential drug candidate that promotes PD-L1 degradation and demonstrate the therapeutic potential of targeting the OTUB1-PD-L1 axis to improve immune checkpoint therapy.

Sixty-eight patients were included; median age was 5 days [1-62]; 95.6% (65/68) were neonates and 23.5% (16/68) premature. Infants with ductal-dependent pulmonary blood flow undergoing ductal stenting may present with a wide range of challenges in the perioperative period. Meticulous care and interdisciplinary coordination are required to optimize the outcomes for this particularly vulnerable patient group.

papers.abstract: It remains unclear if intraoperative hemodynamic therapy should be guided by cardiac index. To evaluate whether individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy vs routine hemodynamic therapy improves outcomes in high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery. This multicenter, single-blind, superiority randomized clinical trial enrolled high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery between October 8, 2023, and October 25, 2025, at 12 university medical centers in Austria, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Germany, and Spain. The date of last follow-up was January 15, 2026. Patients were randomized to individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index vs routine hemodynamic therapy (with blinded cardiac index monitoring). The primary outcome was a composite of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Of the 1128 patients enrolled, 1111 were randomized and 1095 were included in the primary analysis (median age, 67 years [IQR, 59-74 years]; 49.4% were female). The primary outcome occurred in 243 of 549 patients (44.3%) in the individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy group vs 256 of 546 patients (46.9%) in the routine hemodynamic therapy group (relative risk, 0.94 [95.1% CI, 0.83-1.08]; P = .38). There were no between-group differences for the incidence of the individual components of the primary outcome within the first 7 postoperative days. Among high-risk patients undergoing elective major abdominal surgery, individualized cardiac index-guided hemodynamic therapy targeting the patient's preoperative resting cardiac index did not reduce the incidence of a composite outcome of acute kidney injury, acute myocardial injury, severe infectious complications, nonfatal cardiac arrest, or death within the first 7 postoperative days compared with routine hemodynamic therapy. papers.abstract: Hypoxia-driven epigenetic remodeling is a critical determinant of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epigenetic mechanisms coordinating hypoxia signaling with tumor microenvironment remodeling remain incompletely understood. Here, by integrating LUAD cell models, murine tumor models, and spatial transcriptomics with reference-based cell-type deconvolution, we identify SATB2 as a previously unrecognized hypoxia-inducible epigenetic regulator in LUAD. HIF-1α, unlike HIF-2α, directly interacts with the promoter of SATB2, promoting its expression in hypoxic environments. Increased levels of SATB2 have been linked to more severe clinical and pathological characteristics as well as poorer outcomes for patients. Mechanistically, SATB2 physically interacts with HIF-1α and p300, while SATB2 loss reduces H3K27 acetylation and elongating RNA polymerase II occupancy at HIF-1 target loci, supporting a model in which SATB2 facilitates HIF-1α-dependent transcriptional elongation and establishes a positive feedback circuit that amplifies hypoxia-responsive transcriptional programs. Spatial transcriptomic analyses further show that SATB2-associated hypoxic programs are preferentially enriched within malignant tumor niches and are associated with remodeling of the local tumor microenvironment. Functionally, SATB2 promotes LUAD growth, metastasis, angiogenesis, and bevacizumab resistance in a HIF-1α-dependent manner, whereas genetic disruption of SATB2 or pharmacological inhibition of p300 enhances sensitivity to anti-angiogenic therapy. Collectively, these findings identify the SATB2-p300-HIF-1α axis as a hypoxia-responsive epigenetic regulatory mechanism linking transcriptional adaptation to malignant progression and resistance to anti-angiogenic therapy, and provide a preclinical rationale for further investigation of this pathway as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUAD.

papers.abstract: Surgical infections are the most common nosocomial infections and cause substantial morbidity and mortality. Operating rooms are relatively clean, but far from sterile. An unknown fraction of infections result from wound contamination by air-borne bacteria. We therefore tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces wound infections and related complications. Operating rooms, our clusters, were each randomized in each 4-week blocks to either active or identical-looking sham supplemental air sterilization. All investigators, clinicians, and patients were fully blinded to treatment. No other aspect of anesthetic or surgical management was proscribed. Intent-to-treat analysis was restricted to adults who had surgery lasting at least an hour without evidence of pre-existing wound infections. We tested the primary hypothesis that supplemental active purification reduces a collapsed (one or more) composite of surgical wound infections, infection-related complications, or death within 30 days after inpatient surgery. Secondarily, we tested the hypothesis that supplemental air purification reduces the same composite after combined inpatient and outpatient surgeries. A total of 110,538 combined inpatients and outpatients were enrolled across 68 operating rooms, with 107,334 qualifying for analysis. At the third interim analysis, the futility boundary on the composite outcome was crossed for inpatients and for all patients. Enrollment thus stopped with 58,938 randomized inpatients. The primary composite outcome occurred in 8.1% (n=2,389) of inpatients randomized to active purification versus 8.2% (n=2,405) with sham purification: odds ratio 0.98 (95%CI: 0.92 to 1.05), P=0.609. Across all patients, the secondary composite outcome occurred in 5.5% (n=2,959 / 53,730) of active purification cases versus 5.6% (n=2,981 / 53,604) sham cases: odds ratio 0.98 (95% CI: 0.93 to 1.05), P=0.669). Treatment effect did not vary over the weeks in the randomized periods. Supplemental active purification did not reduce surgical wound infections or mortality in surgical patients. papers.abstract: Postoperative increases in plasma total tau (t-tau) protein have raised concerns that surgery can cause CNS injury. Brain-derived tau (BD-tau) is a novel biomarker that quantifies CNS-derived tau. We assessed BD-tau concentrations in plasma and CSF after surgery to investigate neuronal injury and mechanisms driving increases in plasma t-tau. This was a substudy of a previous prospective cohort study enrolling adult patients undergoing hip and knee arthroplasty. We measured plasma and CSF BD-tau and t-tau before neuraxial anaesthesia (baseline) and at 4, 8, 24, 32, and 48 h after surgery and assessed cognitive performance at baseline and 3 months. Biomarker concentrations are reported as median (IQR) percentage change from baseline. Plasma BD-tau peaked at 4 h with a 254% increase (137-382%, P<0.001) and remained elevated by 31% (6-75%, P<0.001) at 48 h. CSF BD-tau was unchanged at 4 h but increased by 51% (21-82%, P=0.004) at 48 h. Plasma BD-tau was associated with plasma t-tau (β=1.09, 95% CI 0.95-1.23, P<0.001), whereas plasma BD-tau and CSF BD-tau were inversely associated (β=-0.71, -0.97 to -0.45, P<0.001). Higher postoperative plasma BD-tau was associated with both higher CSF albumin and worse cognitive performance at 3 months. Early postoperative increases in plasma t-tau are consistent with a CNS origin but not concomitant neuronal injury. Instead, the early plasma BD-tau increase and the inverse association between CSF and plasma BD-tau could indicate a redistribution of tau from the CNS to plasma.

papers.abstract: Calcium- and calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) is highly enriched in dendritic spines at concentrations comparable to those of cytoskeletal proteins and plays a central role in synaptic plasticity. During long-term potentiation, CaMKIIα further accumulates in spines. However, the mechanisms governing its higher-order organization remain poorly understood. Here, we use high-speed atomic force microscopy to visualize interholoenzyme interaction of CaMKIIα at mesoscopic scales (5 to 500 nanometers). Under freely diffusible conditions, CaMKIIα holoenzymes do not form stable clusters. In contrast, when spatially confined, they assemble into chain-like clusters mediated by kinase-domain interactions. These clusters expand upon activation, concomitant with the dissociation of the regulatory segment. Notably, the CaMKIIα Pro 212 →Leu (P212L) mutant associated with neurodevelopmental disorders forms extensive clusters even in the basal state. Together, our findings demonstrate that CaMKIIα-CaMKIIα interactions drive mesoscale cluster formation and that precise regulation of cluster size and activation-dependent growth might be critical for synaptic signaling.

papers.abstract: Importance Blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer disease, particularly plasma phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217), accurately reflect early Alzheimer disease brain pathology in cognitively unimpaired individuals, but estimates of absolute risk of progression to cognitive impairment across multiple cohorts are needed. Objective To estimate absolute risk of progression to cognitive impairment and rates of cognitive decline based on plasma p-tau217 across cognitively unimpaired older adults. Design, Setting, and Participants Longitudinal cohort study using harmonized data from 2684 cognitively unimpaired older adults (defined within cohort) across 6 observational and clinical trial cohorts based in North America, Japan, and Australia. The earliest enrollment was in 2004, with most recent follow-up in 2025. Exposure Baseline plasma p-tau217. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was time to progression to cognitive impairment (mild cognitive impairment, dementia, or 2 consecutive global Clinical Dementia Rating scores ≥0.5). The secondary outcome was longitudinal change on the latent Preclinical Alzheimer Cognitive Composite (PACC; higher values indicate better performance). Results Among the 2684 participants (median [IQR] age, 69.6 [66.2-74.2] years; 1697 [63%] female), there were 478 events of progression to cognitive impairment over a median follow-up of 5.4 years (maximum follow-up of 13.5 years). Each 1-SD increase in baseline p-tau217 level was associated with an increased risk of progression to cognitive impairment (hazard ratio, 1.38 [95% CI, 1.30-1.46]), and the association remained significant after adjustment, including β-amyloid positron emission tomography scan Centiloids (hazard ratio, 1.32 [95% CI, 1.24-1.41]). Participants with high (1.1-2.4 SD) and very high (&gt;2.5 SD) baseline p-tau217 had 24% (95% CI, 20%-28%) and 38% (95% CI, 33%-43%) absolute risk of progression over 5 years, respectively, and risk was markedly higher over 10 years, although longer-term estimates were constrained by limited data. Elevated p-tau217 was also associated with faster cognitive decline based on change in latent PACC score. Among the overall sample, baseline latent PACC scores ranged from −0.8 to 2.7. The 5-year annualized decline for the very high p-tau217 group was −0.07 latent PACC units/y (95% CI, −0.10 to −0.05), relative to 0.03 units/y (95% CI, 0.02-0.04) in the low p-tau217 group. Conclusions and Relevance In a pooled sample of multiple selected cohorts of cognitively unimpaired older adults, higher plasma p-tau217 levels were consistently associated with increased risk of clinical progression and accelerated cognitive decline. By providing time-specific absolute risk estimates, these findings support the potential of p-tau217 for prognostic model development, with direct implications for future trial design. Further validation in unselected populations is needed to inform individual prognosis and clinical decision-making in cognitively unimpaired individuals.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The effect of geographical accessibility to care and patients' social environment on survival has been little studied for hematological malignancies. The objective was to investigate the influence of these factors on excess mortality for these patients in France. This study included 13 French cancer registries. Hodgkin's lymphomas, myeloid haemopathies, multiple myeloma, chronic lymphatic leukemia, diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma and follicular lymphoma diagnosed between 2013 and 2015 are included ( N = 19,041). Social environment was measured using the European Deprivation Index. The access of secondary care was measured by travel time to the nearest reference care center, and access to primary care was estimated using Spatial Accessibility multiscALar (SCALe) index and Accessibilité Potentielle Localisée (APL). The effects of these indicators on excess mortality were investigated using additive excess hazard models with multidimensional penalized splines. For myeloid haemopathies, only the social environment had a significant effect on excess mortality. For diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma, the travel time to nearest reference care center had an impact on excess mortality. Finally, for follicular lymphoma, an increase of APL index was associated with a decrease of mortality. Our study showed that the social environment and the geographical accessibility to care were prognostic factors for survival in certain hematological malignancies.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T‐cell lymphoma (MEITL) is a rare, aggressive intestinal T‐cell lymphoma with poorly defined prognostic factors and limited therapeutic evidence. This study presents a retrospective, pooled patient‐level analysis of MEITL cases, including those previously classified as type II enteropathy‐associated T‐cell lymphoma, consistent with modern MEITL criteria. Among 299 patients, the median age was 60 years, with a male preponderance. Cases clustered predominantly in East Asia. Abdominal pain was the most frequent presentation, and perforation occurred in 31.9% of cases. The canonical CD3+, CD4−, CD5−, CD8+, CD56+ phenotype was present in 65.9% of fully annotated cases. Median OS was 12 months, and median PFS was 5 months. Elevated LDH ≥ 250 U/L ( p = 0.002), advanced Lugano stage II2/IIE/IV ( p = 0.042), and non‐ileal‐only disease distribution were associated with inferior OS, whereas isolated ileal involvement was favorable ( p = 0.004). In multivariable analysis, advanced Lugano stage, non‐ileal‐only involvement, and failure to achieve complete or partial response remained independently adverse. An exploratory prognostic score incorporating stage, anatomic distribution, and LDH showed preliminary risk group separation in a small subset of patients (C‐index 0.734). Stem cell transplantation (SCT) was associated with improved survival in fixed‐time analyses, but this association was attenuated after accounting for transplant timing; exploratory responder‐restricted and landmark analyses suggested that any potential SCT benefit may be concentrated among patients with chemotherapy‐sensitive disease. MEITL demonstrates poor survival despite multimodality therapy. Disease extent, anatomic distribution, LDH, treatment response, and response‐adapted SCT may inform risk stratification and management.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT The craniofacial region represents a distinct yet poorly understood pattern of extranodal involvement in diffuse large B‐cell lymphoma (DLBCL). However, the prognostic significance and molecular characteristics of craniofacial involvement in extranodal DLBCL (EN‐DLBCL) remain unclear. This study included 164 patients with EN‐DLBCL, comprising 98 with craniofacial involvement (CFI) and 66 without. Prognostic factors and survival, as well as relapse and other clinical factors, were analyzed. Targeted next‐generation sequencing was performed in 87 cases. Patients with CFI had significantly inferior 5‐year progression‐free survival ( p = 0.0097) and overall survival ( p = 0.0088), and CFI remained an independent adverse prognostic factor after adjustment for International Prognostic Index (IPI). Sequencing showed that MYD88 , TMSB4X , and PCLO mutations were more frequent in the CFI group. Among the recurrently mutated genes in patients with CFI, only BTG2 mutation was associated with both inferior PFS and OS, whereas no significant prognostic effect was observed in patients without CFI. Immunohistochemistry further demonstrated significantly lower BTG2 expression in BTG2 ‐mutant samples than in wild‐type samples ( p = 0.008). These findings indicate that CFI defines a clinically unfavorable subset of EN‐DLBCL with distinct molecular features and that BTG2 alteration may serve as a candidate biomarker for risk stratification in this setting.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple targeted agents are available for first‐line treatment of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), yet the absence of mature head‐to‐head comparisons makes treatment selection challenging. The prospective, multicenter FIRST‐CLL study evaluated real‐world treatment allocation, and the contribution of biological, clinical, logistical and patient‐related factors to first‐line regimen choice in Italy. 285 consecutive patients with CLL/small lymphocytic lymphoma initiating first‐line therapy across 13 Centers were included. Treating physicians rated predefined variables guiding treatment selection using the 5‐point relevance score . Overall, 116 patients (41%) received continuous Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi), 114 (40%) ibrutinib plus venetoclax (IV), and 55 (19%) venetoclax plus obinutuzumab (VO). Continuous BTKi were more frequently prescribed in older and comorbid patients, whereas IV was preferentially used in younger individuals. TP53 disruption was associated with BTKi use, while mutated immunoglobulin heavy chain status was common in patients receiving VO. According to relevance scores , age, treatment duration and administration route, and patient preference were the most influential determinants of treatment selection. Comorbidity burden additionally guided BTKi prescription, whereas molecular features were more relevant in the selection of fixed‐duration regimens. This study offers a real‐world quantitative assessment of treatment decision drivers in frontline CLL, offering a data‐driven framework to interpret clinical decision‐making.

papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo‐HCT) is the only curative approach for adult T‐cell leukemia‐lymphoma (ATL). However, preventing post‐transplant relapse remains challenging. While pre‐transplant disease status is known to be associated with post‐transplant outcomes, the impact of residual disease (RD) localization at the time of allo‐HCT has not been well described. In this retrospective study of 33 patients with aggressive ATL who underwent allo‐HCT, patients were classified into two risk groups based on RD sites: a low‐risk group (no lymph node [LN] or extranodal [EN] disease, regardless of the presence of peripheral blood disease) and a high‐risk group (presence of LN and/or EN disease). The low‐risk group had significantly superior overall survival (OS) and progression‐free survival (PFS) compared to the high‐risk group, with longer median survival times (OS: 1953 vs. 245 days; PFS: 1177.5 vs. 72 days) and higher 2‐year survival rates (OS: 65.0% vs. 11.3%; PFS: 50.0% vs. 8.3%) ( p = 0.012 and p = 0.013, respectively). Furthermore, even among patients who had not achieved complete response, RD localization stratified the survival outcomes: the 2‐year OS and PFS were 75.0% and 75.0% in the low‐risk group, compared with 11.3% and 8.3% in the high‐risk group, respectively. In conclusion, RD localization at the time of allo‐HCT is a novel prognostic factor, highlighting the need for tailored pre‐transplant management for ATL.
