papers.abstract: Metabolic adaptation is often driven by mutations in pleiotropic genes that affect metabolism globally. However, identifying which phenotypes produced by such mutations drive selection remains difficult. Here, we consider metabolite correlation networks as a systems-level phenotype whose emergent properties reflect the combined effects of biochemical reactions and regulation. We hypothesize that mutation-induced changes in the covariance structure of these networks constitute complex phenotypes linking genetic change to bacterial fitness, and that node-level shifts can identify metabolites and pathways mechanistically associated with adaptation. We test this hypothesis by applying adaptive laboratory evolution to a metabolically suboptimal Escherichia coli strain in which metK, encoding methionine adenosyltransferase (MAT), is replaced by an ortholog from Ureaplasma urealyticum. Untargeted metabolite correlation networks reveal that evolution shifts S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), the MAT product, from a peripheral node to a key connector between network clusters. None of the accumulated pleiotropic mutations causing the shift directly affect MAT activity or SAM metabolism, indicating that this transition emerges from system-level metabolic reorganization. Targeted metabolomics of nodes showing similar shifts identifies additional metabolites involved in SAM-related pathways. These findings establish metabolite correlation networks as a framework for mapping genotype-phenotype-fitness relationships and prioritizing metabolic nodes linked to adaptive mechanisms.

papers.abstract: We report the first case of using teclistamab, a BCMA × CD3 bispecific antibody, in a 63-year-old male with κ-light chain deposition disease (LCDD) involving the kidneys and probably the heart. The patient initially responded to daratumumab-pomalidomide-dexamethasone but experienced hematologic relapse. Salvage therapy with teclistamab induced a rapid and sustained hematologic complete response without cytokine release syndrome or neurotoxicity. Renal and cardiac functions remained stable. This case provides critical early evidence that BCMA-directed immunotherapy may serve as an effective salvage strategy for this rare plasma cell disorder, addressing a significant unmet therapeutic need.

papers.abstract: Nucleotide excision repair (NER) is a critical DNA repair pathway responsible for removing bulky, helix-distorting DNA lesions, including ultraviolet radiation-induced photoproducts and platinum drug-DNA adducts. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current understanding of NER in cancer, with particular emphasis on its role in therapeutic response. We discuss the molecular mechanisms of DNA repair in cancer, the significance of NER in platinum-based therapies, results from in vitro studies across various cancer types, findings from patient-based studies, and outcomes from clinical trials. Special attention is given to ERCC1, ERCC2/XPD, XPA, and XPC molecules as potential biomarkers of treatment response and therapeutic targets, and incorporating the most recent discoveries regarding NER inhibitors, mutational signatures, and synthetic lethality-based approaches.

papers.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) is a leading cause of anovulatory infertility. Although follicular developmental arrest is a defining feature of PMOS, the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility, endocrine imbalance and follicular microenvironmental dysfunction remain incompletely understood, particularly across clinical subtypes. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of preovulatory follicular-fluid cells from healthy controls and women with uncomplicated PMOS, hyperandrogenic PMOS and metformin-treated insulin-resistant PMOS. We integrated these data with GWAS-derived disease relevance scores and ovarian chromatin-accessibility annotations to map genetic risk to follicular cell populations and regulatory programmes. Ligand-receptor analyses were used to infer intercellular communication networks. Transcriptomic metabolic findings were further assessed by follicular-fluid metabolic and steroid-hormone measurements, DHT-treated granulosa-cell functional assays, and reanalysis of a DHEA-induced mouse PMOS-like ovarian dataset. We generated a single-cell atlas of the PMOS follicular microenvironment comprising 220,983 high-quality cells. Granulosa cells showed the strongest enrichment of PMOS-related genetic risk, with regulatory-genetic support from ovarian snATAC-seq integration. Among granulosa cell states, a GC2_CYP19A1⁺ population was preferentially associated with hyperandrogenic PMOS and displayed a transcriptional programme characterized by steroidogenic remodelling coupled to reduced energy-metabolic activity. Biochemical profiling supported this endocrine-metabolic imbalance, showing increased follicular-fluid androstenedione (ASD) and estrone, reduced estradiol and E2/ASD ratio, decreased ATP, citrate and fumarate hydratase activity, and increased lactate and β-hydroxybutyrate. Prolonged DHT exposure impaired granulosa-cell mitochondrial respiration, ATP production and mitochondrial membrane potential. In parallel, PMOS subtypes showed immune remodelling and altered ligand-receptor signalling, with hyperandrogenic PMOS associated with increased inflammatory signalling and reduced homeostatic or tissue-repair pathways. Reanalysis of a DHEA-induced mouse ovarian dataset provided supportive evidence for androgen-associated steroidogenic pathway perturbation. This study provides a cell-resolved framework linking PMOS genetic susceptibility to endocrine-metabolic and immune remodelling in the preovulatory follicular microenvironment. The identification of a hyperandrogen-associated GC2_CYP19A1⁺ state highlights a candidate cellular programme in which steroidogenic imbalance is coupled to impaired granulosa-cell bioenergetics. These findings provide a resource for future validation and may inform microenvironment-guided stratification of PMOS and the development of strategies aimed at restoring follicular function.

papers.abstract: Drug resistance is a major cause of treatment failure in breast cancer patients. Numerous genetic and epigenetic markers have been proposed to influence Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy (NACT) response, and genes that regulate the effectiveness of chemotherapeutic agents undergo expression regulation via methylation. In this study, we aimed to investigate the methylation levels of KDM5A, KDM5B, and KDM5C, as well as their associated genes, EZH2, TFAP2C, ZMYND8, and SIN3B (Exon 1-2 and 19-20), in blood samples collected from patients before and after NACT treatment. Besides, we also examined potential variations in the KDM5A, KDM5B, and KDM5C gene regions. Twenty patients were diagnosed with breast cancer, and 30 healthy control individuals were included in the study. Blood samples were taken from the patients twice, before and after NACT. Methylation levels of KDM5 family genes and related genes were analyzed using Methylation-specific PCR (MSP). Additionally, potential variants in the KDM5A, KDM5B, and KDM5C gene regions were identified using Sanger sequencing. According to the methylation analysis results, the SIN3B (Exon 19-20), KDM5C, EZH2, and TFAP2C genes were prominent in patients with pathological partial response, while the KDM5A, KDM5B, KDM5C, EZH2, TFAP2C, and SIN3B (Exon 19-20) genes were prominent in patients with pathological complete response. According to genotyping results, rs41308616 and rs971896841 variants were detected as heterozygous in the KDM5C gene region in two patients, respectively. The methylation percentages and genetic variations in the KDM5 family and related gene regions identified in this study may serve as potential biomarkers for developing treatment strategies for breast cancer patients.

papers.abstract: Various social determinants of health (SDOH) have been shown to negatively impact breast cancer outcomes. Though there are recommendations for comprehensive SDOH assessment, little is known about the optimal frequency of reassessments and change in health-related social needs (HRSN) over time for specific patient populations. We sought to characterize SDOH screening and HRSN patterns among patients with breast cancer in a safety-net system. A retrospective study was conducted to evaluate SDOH survey responses in the electronic medical records and screening frequency from patients diagnosed with breast cancer between January 2021 to January 2024 at Parkland Health. There were 566 patients diagnosed with breast cancer with a mean age at diagnosis of 55.0 (standard deviation, SD: 11.4) years. There were 54 (9.5%) with Stage IV breast cancer. Patients were initially at risk for 1.36 (SD: 1.39) out of the 11 HRSN domains. Patients completed an average 17.3 (SD: 8.9) out of 28 questions on initial survey. The most common risk domains identified were Alcohol Use and Food Insecurity. No patients were screened for Interpersonal Violence. The median time from initial survey to first change in risk level for any domain was 8.7 months. Patients with Stage IV disease underwent fewer SDOH re-screenings compared to patients with Stage I, II, and III disease (p < 0.001). Within our system, greater attention should be placed towards fully assessing patients' HRSN and screening for interpersonal violence. SDOH screening at 6-month intervals may help to capture changes in HSRNs and assess the impact of resource interventions.

papers.abstract: Advancements in human epidermal growth factor (HER)-targeted therapy have significantly improved survival in patients with de novo metastatic HER-2 positive (HER2+) breast cancer (dnMBC). The role of breast surgery is debated. We examined which HER2 + dnMBC patients undergo surgery and compared outcomes to systemic therapy alone. We performed a single institution retrospective review of patients with HER2 + dnMBC diagnosed 2011-2023. Data included demographics, clinicopathologic details, treatment information, local and distant disease progression, and survival outcomes. Analyses included logistic regression, Kaplan Meier, and Cox proportional hazards models. The study included 103 patients. Of these, 42.7% underwent breast surgery (70.5% mastectomy, 29.5% lumpectomy). Of these, 72.7% underwent axillary surgery (38.6% axillary lymph node dissection, 27.3% sentinel lymph node biopsy, 6.8% targeted axillary dissection). The median age at diagnosis was 48 years (surgery) and 56 years (no surgery) (p = 0.10). The surgery group had lower number of metastatic sites (1.3 vs. 1.9, p = 0.003) and exhibited higher rates of local disease progression pre-operatively (39% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.05). Post-operatively, there was no significant difference in local disease progression (17.1% vs. 23.5%, p = 0.42). After adjusting for age, sites of metastases, and number of metastatic sites, those who underwent surgery had improved overall survival (HR 0.33 (0.14-0.77), p = 0.02). Patients with HER2 + dnMBC with lower metastatic disease burden and local disease progression were more likely to undergo breast surgery. There was no significant difference in local disease control post-operatively. The significant association between surgery and improved survival must be interpreted with caution due selection bias in this retrospective study.

papers.abstract: The interval between breast cancer diagnosis and surgery is psychologically demanding, and meeting the Swedish standardised care pathway target has remained challenging. We examined whether diagnosis-to-surgery lead time is associated with patient-reported psychological outcomes. We conducted a longitudinal cohort study using Swedish National Quality Register for Breast Cancer data (2020-2024). The cohort comprised 2,906 women with primary invasive breast cancer undergoing surgery, with patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) data at baseline (n = 2,906), 6 months (n = 2,638), and 12 months (n = 2,678). Lead time from biopsy to surgery was modelled continuously (per 1 SD ≈ 19 days). The primary outcome was worry about future health (EORTC QLQ-BR23 item 43); secondary outcomes were general worry, tension, depressed mood, and overall quality of life. Associations were estimated using mixed-effects cumulative link models adjusted for clinical and tumour factors, pandemic era, patient, and healthcare region. Median lead time was 32 days (IQR 23-42). Longer lead time was associated with greater worry about future health (adjusted OR 1.15 per SD, 95% CI 1.04-1.27), while associations with the secondary outcomes were smaller and not statistically significant. At baseline, high future-health worry was more common with lead times > 35 vs. ≤ 35 days (42.2% vs. 35.1%). Longer diagnosis-to-surgery lead time was associated with greater future-health worry, with smaller, non-significant associations for general distress and quality of life. The findings highlight the preoperative waiting period as a potential context for improved communication about expected timelines and reasons for delay.

papers.abstract: De-escalation has become standard across breast cancer management. Many early-stage HR+/HER2-negative breast cancers are eligible for both SLNB omission and accelerated partial breast irradiation (APBI). However, the oncologic safety of dual de-escalation has not been evaluated except in patients ≥ 70 years. We sought to characterize national practice patterns and factors associated with adoption of this dual de-escalation approach. Women aged 50-69 years with clinical T1-T2N0 breast cancer who underwent upfront breast-conserving surgery between (2012 - 2022) were identified from the National Cancer Database. Patients were categorized by axillary surgery and by adjuvant radiation modality (WBI, APBI, or none). We assessed trends and factors associated with de-escalation. 316,324 patients met inclusion criteria, of whom 98% underwent SLNB. Among patients who underwent SLNB, 83% received WBI, 11% received APBI, and 6% received no radiation. In contrast, among patients in whom SLNB was omitted, 63% received WBI, 8% received APBI, and 30% received no radiation. SLNB omission remained low throughout the study period at < 3%, while APBI use increased from 8% to 16.5%. Dual de-escalation was rarely performed throughout the study period remaining < 0.30%. Shared predictors of de-escalation included cT1 tumors, ductal histology, low grade, and treatment at academic/research programs. These findings highlight the need for prospective studies to define the safety, outcomes, and patient selection criteria for combined de-escalation strategies. Until these data are available, patient-centered discussions are essential to determine the most appropriate strategy for patients with low-risk disease.

papers.abstract: Germline genetic testing is increasing. While testing barriers are well characterized, less is known about post-testing needs and utilization of screening and prevention resources by women with pathogenic variants (PVs) in breast cancer susceptibility genes. A 38-question online survey was developed by Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered (FORCE), a patient advocacy group, and administered electronically to subscribers from February-May 2024. Study eligibility criteria included female sex and a germline PV conferring elevated lifetime risk of breast cancer (ATM, BARD1, BRCA1, BRCA2, CDH1, CHEK2, PALB2, PTEN, RAD51C, RAD51D, STK11, or TP53). Of 1,025 respondents who initiated the survey, 937 were women. Most were non-Hispanic White (91.7%) and from the United States (81.6%). The most common PVs were BRCA2 (31.4%), BRCA1 (25.5%) and CHEK2 (9.2%). The most frequently used resources were education and information services about medical options (39.3%) and peer support (28.1%). Few respondents used financial navigation (4.0%) or financial support (5.3%), but up to 45% reported needing these services. Among breast screening users (53.8% used mammogram, 42.2% magnetic resonance imaging, 19.4% ultrasound), 37.8% found it hard to prepare emotionally for results and 14% found it hard to pay for screening. One-third (37.1%) of respondents found deciding whether to have risk-reducing mastectomy hard; two-thirds (64.0%) found physical recovery hard, more than half (60.2%) found emotional recovery hard, and one-quarter (24.7%) found paying for risk-reducing mastectomy hard. In this contemporary sample of women at elevated risk of breast cancer, more than one-third had unmet financial needs and up to two-thirds had difficulty with screening or risk-reducing surgery. Closing these gaps will be essential to improve outcomes for women with hereditary breast cancer.

papers.abstract: High-volume hospitals deliver improved outcomes for patients with breast cancer, supporting referrals for breast cancer surgical care to high-volume regional facilities. This retrospective cohort study investigated how multidisciplinary cancer care trajectories and patient care experiences varied by surgical facility classification (regional vs. community as a proxy for high- vs. low-volume) and whether effects differed by rural-residence. We used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Consumer Assessment of Healthcare Providers and Systems (SEER-CAHPS) data for Medicare beneficiaries who received surgery for non-metastatic breast cancer from 2009 to 2019. We mapped cancer care trajectories using facility classification and oncologist specialty and performed state sequence analysis to identify care trajectory clusters. We used linear mixed-effects models to examine associations of surgical facility classification with patient-reported experience measures and assessed effect modification by rurality. Of the 3,327 patients in our cohort, 15.4% were rural-residing and 68.8% received surgery at a regional facility. Care trajectories indicated that patients tended to receive adjuvant care from the same type of facility as their surgical treatment. Patients who received surgery at community facilities (vs. regional) were significantly more likely to report better experiences with getting needed care (Est. (95%CI) = 3.5 (0.10,6.9), p = 0.043), with no significant differences for getting care quickly, care coordination, or doctor communication. Rural-residence was not a significant effect modifier. Receiving surgery at community facilities is associated with better patient-reported experiences for getting needed care. Moreover, surgical facility classification appears to influence the setting for subsequent cancer care, which may impact patient experiences in getting needed care. Not applicable.

papers.abstract: Endometrial stromal sarcomas (ESSs) comprise a heterogeneous group of uterine mesenchymal tumors characterized by diverse morphological features and recurrent molecular alterations. Although molecular classification has substantially improved ESS diagnosis, the relationship between specific genetic alterations and morphological phenotypes remains incompletely understood. We performed an integrated molecular and histopathological analysis of ESS to investigate genotype-phenotype correlations and refine tumor classification. A total of 61 patients with histologically suspected ESSs were initially enrolled, and 51 successfully underwent targeted RNA sequencing, followed by comprehensive morphological reassessment, immunohistochemical evaluation, molecular validation, and clinicopathological correlation. Molecularly confirmed ESSs demonstrated distinct genotype-associated morphological patterns. PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs showed a strong association with hypocellular growth and prominent collagenized stroma. Quantitative cellularity analysis further demonstrated significantly lower tumor cellularity in PHF1-rearranged low-grade ESSs compared with JAZF1::SUZ12-rearranged tumors (p < 0.001). High-grade ESSs with YWHAE::NUTM2 and BCOR::ZC3H7B alterations showed higher mitotic activity than low-grade ESSs and demonstrated tongue-like infiltration patterns in both primary and metastatic lesions, indicating that this growth pattern, traditionally emphasized in low-grade ESSs, may represent a broader morphological feature of ESSs. Molecular reassessment led to the reclassification of 10 cases (19.6%, 10/51), identifying tumors with alternative molecular alterations that were initially diagnosed as ESSs based on morphology alone. Among these cases, a uterine sarcoma harboring a novel GATA6::SRF fusion exhibited a low-grade ESS-like morphological phenotype but lacked the characteristic molecular alterations of conventional ESSs, suggesting a potential molecularly defined uterine sarcoma subtype requiring further investigation. Our findings demonstrate that integrated molecular and histopathological analysis extends beyond diagnostic refinement by revealing genotype-phenotype relationships, expanding the molecular spectrum of ESSs and ESS-like uterine sarcomas, and providing new insights into the biological heterogeneity of these rare tumors. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Goldilocks-based breast reconstruction (GBR) offers an autologous, implant-free option for patients seeking breast mound restoration after mastectomy. It is particularly suited for patients with macromastia, ptosis, or significant comorbidities. Despite its growing adoption, limited studies have examined patient understanding and expectations. We interviewed patients who underwent GBR after mastectomy within our institution. Demographic, oncologic, and perioperative data were collected. Semi-structured interviews were conducted to explore patient understanding, decision making process and post-operative experience based on Ottawa Decision Support Framework. Nine participants were included. Mean age was 58.1 years (range: 41-71), and mean body mass index was 34.9 kg/m2 (range: 24.3-46.1). Most participants demonstrated a good understanding of the procedure and why it was offered. Common reasons for selecting this approach were a desire to avoid implants and additional surgeries. Misunderstandings regarding the amount of residual breast tissue, expected postoperative volume, and the need for post-mastectomy surveillance contributed to dissatisfaction. However, decisional regrets were rare. Motivations for choosing GBR consistently revolve around avoidance of implant placement and desire for single-stage surgery. Common misconceptions regarding the extent of oncological resection and expectations for achievable volume from GBR should be addressed pre-operatively.

papers.abstract: Recurrence risk after hepatectomy for colorectal liver metastases (CRLMs) changes during follow-up, but whether baseline tumor burden remains prognostically relevant with increasing recurrence-free time is unclear. We evaluated the time-dependent prognostic relevance of liver metastasis number. We retrospectively analyzed 226 patients who underwent initial curative-intent hepatectomy for CRLMs between 2007 and 2022. Three-year conditional recurrence-free survival (RFS) was estimated at surgery and after 6, 12, and 24 months without recurrence. Landmark Cox models evaluated liver metastasis number (< 4 vs. ≥ 4), adjusting for RAS status, with supplementary expanded models. Three-year conditional RFS improved from 27.1% at surgery to 33.3%, 49.3%, and 76.6% after 6, 12, and 24 months without recurrence, respectively. However, subsequent RFS remained worse in patients with ≥ 4 liver metastases at the 6-month (adjusted hazard ratio [HR]: 1.83, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.14-2.94; p = 0.012) and 12-month (HR: 2.14, 95% CI: 1.08-4.27; p = 0.030) landmarks. In supplementary expanded models, the associations remained directionally similar but were attenuated. Recurrence risk improved with increasing recurrence-free time, but survivors remained heterogeneous according to baseline tumor burden. Liver metastasis number retained prognostic relevance at early postoperative landmarks.

papers.abstract: Hepatic adenomas (HAs) are rare benign liver tumors traditionally associated with young women, yet contemporary epidemiologic trends reveal increasing recognition among men. Historically, universal resection in males has been recommended because of a nearly tenfold increased risk of malignant transformation as reported by Farges et al. in a single-institution surgical series; however, advances in molecular profiling and imaging have challenged this paradigm. β-catenin-activated and inflammatory subtypes account for most cases in men, often associated with anabolic steroid exposure, obesity, or metabolic syndrome. β-catenin-activated adenomas-particularly those harboring CTNNB1 exon 3 mutations-demonstrate the strongest correlation with malignant potential. Magnetic resonance imaging with hepatobiliary contrast agents can suggest subtype but lacks perfect accuracy; biopsy offers improved diagnostic precision and enables molecular confirmation. Current ACG and EASL guidelines still endorse routine resection for all hepatic adenomas in males; however, available retrospective data suggest that malignant transformation appears to be uncommon in small (5 cm) lesions lacking exon 3 CTNNB1 mutations; however, this observation is derived from limited, predominantly retrospective data and does not exclude the possibility of malignant transformation in this subgroup. These data support selective, biopsy-guided surveillance for small, indeterminate tumors within experienced multidisciplinary centers where longitudinal follow-up is reliable. Resection remains the standard recommendation for large or β-catenin-mutated adenomas, with minimally invasive surgery demonstrating excellent outcomes. Modern management of hepatic adenomas in men should be individualized, integrating molecular subtype, size, risk factors, and patient context. A multidisciplinary and molecularly informed strategy is essential to optimize outcomes while avoiding unnecessary intervention.

papers.abstract: Abstract Ciliary microtubule doublets, consisting of an incomplete B-tubule on the surface of a complete A-microtubule, form the fundamental structural framework of motile and sensory cilia/flagella. Ciliary proteins PACRG and FAP20, which are essential for flagellar stability and function, localize to the junction between the A- and the B-tubule. However, their precise role in microtubule doublet assembly and dynamics remains unknown. Here, using a cell-free assay, TIRF-microscopy, and cryo-electron tomography, we demonstrate that in combination PACRG and FAP20 stabilize B-tubule dynamics and microtubule doublet architecture. We show that together these proteins localize to the B-tubules in distinct, high-density patches, which locally stabilize B-tubule by decreasing its depolymerization velocity and increasing its rescue frequency. Cryo-tomography of in vitro reconstructed microtubule doublets in presence of PACRG and FAP20 reveals reduced B-tubule curvature fluctuations, promoting a more rigid and aligned conformation. Altogether, our findings suggest that PACRG and FAP20 function synergistically to reinforce microtubule doublet stability, ensuring ciliary integrity and function.

papers.abstract: Liver-organotropic metastasis occurs in cancers such as uveal melanoma (UM) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and is a leading cause of mortality at the terminal stage. Colonization is a rate-limiting and converging step in the metastatic cascade. The drivers underlying liver colonization have largely remained elusive. In this report, we hypothesized that pioneer transcription factors (TFs) increase chromatin accessibility and superenhancer (SE) remodeling, which subsequently promote colonization-associated cellular features [e.g., proliferation, survival, cancer stem cells (CSCs), motility] by driving the transcription of the respective SE-associated genes. We tested this hypothesis and discovered that the pioneer TF KLF4 promoted chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling by ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq. Chromatin accessibility and SE remodeling significantly increased the transcription of the SE-associated genes MCL1 and RASGRP3, which consequently promoted proliferation, motility, and metastasis. Furthermore, the upregulation of KLF4 expression in UM cells was promoted by RN7SL2-containing exosomes from surrounding endothelial cells. Analysis of clinical datasets revealed that the overexpression of RIG-I, STAT1, KLF4, and RASGRP3 was individually correlated with shorter metastasis-free survival or overall survival in patients with UM and PDAC. In conclusion, the identification of the exoRN7SL2-STAT1-KLF4-SEs-RASGRP3 signaling axis may help elucidate metastatic colonization through interactions between tumor cells and the endothelial niche and may yield novel and viable therapeutic targets.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Sonic hedgehog (SHH) medulloblastoma (MB) accounts for approximately one-third of all MB cases, the most common malignant brain tumor in children. Despite therapy, SHH MB relapse is frequent and has a dismal prognosis. New treatments for recurrent SHH MB are needed; however, the molecular drivers of relapse are poorly understood. Methods We profiled 22 SHH MB specimens (16 primary and 6 recurrent), including four primary–recurrent patient pairs, using overlapping single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq; n = 16), single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (snATAC-seq; n = 13), and spatial transcriptomic ( n = 6) cohorts. We integrated these data with exome-derived variant calls from 25 specimens, including seven patients with primary and recurrent samples. Bulk RNA-seq data from 48 specimens representing 24 primary–recurrent pairs were used for validation. Results Our analyses show evidence of positive selection for nonsynonymous tumor mutations, including TP53 mutations involving its DNA-binding and tetramerization domains. TP53 mutations were associated with reduced base-excision repair (BER) gene expression and accessibility of linked cis-regulatory regions. Recurrent tumors showed increased tumor mutational burden (TMB) and an endoplasmic-reticulum (ER) stress expression program associated with poorer survival. Angiogenic gene expression and inferred immunosuppressive myeloid signaling were increased in recurrent disease. Conclusions These data define recurrence-associated cellular and regulatory programs, nominate candidate therapeutic targets and prognostic markers, and provide a single-cell and spatial atlas of SHH MB.

papers.abstract: Interventional procedures are commonly used to diagnose and treat chronic pain of spinal origin but guidance on: their indications; frequency; technical conduct; requirements for image guidance; outcome measurement; and management of complications is lacking. These guidelines were developed by a Canadian group of clinicians, researchers, patient partners and representatives from provincial healthcare regulatory and funding bodies. Reviews of published literature were undertaken for commonly performed spinal procedures for pain, and the evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Evidence-based recommendations for each procedure were graded on a scale from A (strongest level) to D (not recommended), or as insufficient (I), using US Preventive Services Task Force criteria with the level of certainty rated as high, medium or low. All consensus recommendations required at least 75% agreement among the guideline panel. Good clinical practice statements were also developed. We provide 15 key recommendations. The guidelines provide clinical practice recommendations and good clinical practice statements for procedures targeting chronic pain originating from the cervical, lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints. Clinical indications, evidence for efficacy and suggested frequency for repeated procedures have also been proposed. These guidelines provide evidence-based recommendations and good clinical practice statements for performing diagnostic and therapeutic spinal interventions for chronic pain.

papers.abstract: Ifupinostat (BEBT-908) is a novel dual-targeted inhibitor of histone deacetylase (HDACs) and phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase alpha (PI3Kα). We evaluated the efficacy and safety of ifupinostat monotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) after at least 2 prior lines of systemic therapy. Eligible participants received intravenous ifupinostat at 22.5 mg/m² on days 1, 3, 5, 8, 10, and 12 of a 21-day cycle. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR) assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR). Secondary endpoints included disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DoR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS) and safety. From June 2020 to July 2022, 128 patients were enrolled and included in the safety set (SS), and 115 patients were in the efficacy analysis set (EAS). At the data cutoff (July 2023), the median follow-up was 19.58 months (95% confidence interval [CI] 16.82-21.95). The ORR was 36.5% (42/115, 95% CI 27.7-46.0), with a complete response rate of 11.3% (13/115). The median DoR was 6.2 months (95% CI 3.5-14.5), median PFS was 2.7 months (95% CI 1.6-3.7), and median OS was 9.9 months (95% CI 7.8-14.8). Treatment-related adverse events (TRAEs) occurred in 99.2% (127/128) of patients, and ≥grade 3 TRAEs in 86.7% (111/128). The most common ≥grade 3 TRAEs were thrombocytopenia (75.8%, 97/128), neutropenia (33.6%, 43/128), and leukopenia (22.7%, 29/128). No treatment-related deaths occurred. Ifupinostat demonstrated promising efficacy and a manageable safety profile as a new therapeutic alternative for patients with r/r DLBCL. Clinical Trial Registry Number: ChiCTR1900028179.

papers.abstract: Targeted therapy has revolutionized the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients harboring oncogenic alterations, and next-generation tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) significantly increase blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, leading to improved disease control and survival benefits. However, several issues remain to be addressed, including the selection of more appropriate and individualized agents, the emergence of TKI resistance, and the challenging management of central nervous system (CNS) progression. In this review, we comprehensively summarize the efficacy and safety of TKIs and targeted specific antibodies in advanced or metastatic patients with common or rare mutations, providing guidance in selecting the optimal agent. We further explore the mechanisms underlying drug resistance and regimens aimed at overcoming resistance. In nonmetastatic resectable or unresectable NSCLC, we discuss the therapeutic potential of targeted agents and current issues requiring further research. In addition, we distinguish current and potential therapeutic strategies for patients with baseline brain metastasis (BM) and those without baseline BM who subsequently develop brain progression, leading to more effective and personalized treatment. Finally, we provide perspectives on challenges and future directions in the identification and treatment of oncogenic alterations, particularly in the context of co-mutations and the heterogeneous nature of metastases, and emphasize the clinical importance of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted genetic testing and biomarker development.

papers.abstract: Infiltration between the popliteal artery and the capsule of the knee (IPACK) and the selective tibial nerve block provide analgesia for the posterior aspect of the knee after total knee arthroplasty. This randomised controlled triple-blinded trial tested the hypothesis that IPACK provides superior analgesia to selective tibial nerve block after total knee arthroplasty. Patients having total knee arthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia with a femoral triangle block were allocated randomly to receive either IPACK with 19 ml ropivacaine 0.2% or a selective tibial nerve block with 5 ml ropivacaine 0.75%. The postoperative analgesic strategy included paracetamol; ibuprofen; and intravenous morphine patient-controlled analgesia. Primary outcome was cumulative intravenous morphine consumption on postoperative day 1. Secondary analgesic outcomes included pain scores at rest and during movement measured on postoperative days 1, 2 and 3. Functional outcomes were quadriceps strength; walking distance; and range of motion. In total, data from 90 patients were analysed (45 allocated to each group). Cumulative intravenous morphine consumption on postoperative day 1 was similar between the patients allocated to the IPACK and selective tibial nerve block groups (mean (SD) 6 (7) mg vs. 5 (6) mg, respectively; p = 0.36). Four patients (9%) who received selective tibial nerve block had motor block of the common peroneal nerve. No other differences were seen between groups in secondary outcomes. The IPACK and selective tibial nerve block provide similar analgesia after total knee arthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia with a femoral triangle block.

papers.abstract: Despite durable clinical responses to immunotherapy in a subset of patients, most solid tumors remain refractory owing to an immune-excluded phenotype characterized by limited trafficking, infiltration, and function of effector immune cells within the tumor microenvironment (TME). Tumor endothelial cells (TECs) function as vascular immune gatekeepers that orchestrate this process. Driven by persistent pro-angiogenic signaling and metabolic stress, TECs establish a multilayered immune barrier through structurally abnormal, poorly perfused vasculature, endothelial anergy, and active immunosuppressive programs. TECs directly suppress effector T-cell and natural killer (NK)-cell function through checkpoint-like ligands, death-ligand pathways, and immunometabolic mechanisms involving adenosine production and tryptophan catabolism. Simultaneously, they recruit, retain, and reprogram immunosuppressive leukocytes, thereby reinforcing immune exclusion and therapeutic resistance. Here, we propose a TEC-centric vascular immune gatekeeping framework and review strategies to reprogram tumor vessels from immune barriers into conduits for effective immune-cell trafficking and activation. We discuss endothelial-directed monotherapies that transiently normalize or reset TEC states, together with combination strategies integrating vascular modulation with immune checkpoint blockade, adoptive and innate immune-cell therapies, cancer vaccines, oncolytic viruses, STING agonists, and multifunctional antibodies. We also highlight key translational considerations, including biomarker-guided patient stratification, pharmacodynamic monitoring using mechanism-based endpoints, and optimization of treatment dose and scheduling within the vascular normalization window. Overall, this review establishes endothelial reprogramming as a central strategy for overcoming vascular immune gatekeeping and provides a mechanistic framework for biomarker-guided vascular-immune combination therapies in solid tumors.

papers.abstract: Abstract Endothelial dysfunction contributes to multi-organ injury in sepsis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here we show that endothelial ubiquitin-specific protease 28 (USP28) is increased in patients with sepsis and in male mice in a murine polymicrobial sepsis model. Mechanistically, USP28 stabilizes non-muscle myosin heavy chain IIA (NMMHC IIA) by removing K48-linked ubiquitination at K1413. Moreover, NMMHC IIA promotes interferon-α/β receptor 1 (IFNAR1) trafficking to the plasma membrane, enhancing IFNAR1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1 (STAT1) signaling and endothelial necroptosis. In turn, STAT1 transcriptionally increases USP28 expression, forming a positive feedback loop. Endothelial USP28 deletion or pharmacological inhibition attenuates sepsis-induced multi-organ injury, whereas USP28 overexpression exacerbates it. Conversely, endothelial NMMHC IIA or IFNAR1 overexpression largely abrogates the protection conferred by USP28 deficiency in septic male mice. These findings identify a USP28–NMMHC IIA axis that promotes endothelial necroptosis and multi-organ injury in sepsis through IFNAR1/STAT1 signaling.

papers.abstract: Abstract Carbon removal and storage is central to many net-zero commitments, yet its durability, particularly for nature-based methods, is uncertain due to disturbance risks. Previous work shows that carbon storage-years (the time-integrated quantity of carbon storage) are proportional to time-integrated avoided warming, which in turn causes avoided changes in slow-responding climate variables. Here, we show that temporary carbon storage results in avoided changes in inertial climate variables. Avoided changes in 2100 are proportional to carbon storage-years across a range of storage amounts and emissions scenarios for permafrost carbon, ocean carbon, Atlantic meridional overturning circulation, ocean temperature, and thermosteric sea-level rise. By 2300, proportionality persists in some variables, notably sea-level rise, ocean temperature, and ocean carbon. Temporary storage therefore has climate benefits that extend beyond the duration of the storage, with some persistence of benefits even on multi-century timescales. We find that these climate benefits are greatest when temporary storage is paired with ambitious mitigation.

papers.abstract: Introduction Reconstructing the jaw after tumor removal or trauma increasingly relies on custom 3D-printed titanium plates. This customization applies to the implant's shape. It usually does not apply to the internal structure. The width and thickness of the plate are still determined by the designer, based on experience and clinical observation. The critical design parameters of the PSI govern its mechanical performance. Hence, if the design could analyze these parameters and adjust them accordingly, it could help avoid plate fracture. This study introduces a parametric-design approach that closes this gap. Methods The proposed algorithm addresses these challenges by using stress data derived from finite element analysis (FEA) to selectively reinforce only the high-stress regions of a reconstruction plate, rather than uniformly reinforcing the entire plate. The reinforcement is smoothly integrated into the plate’s geometry to prevent abrupt changes in cross-section that could create stress concentrations. The approach was applied to a baseline plate at two regions of elevated stress. Results and discussion Plate A reinforced only the primary zone; this reduced peak stress by 36.0% and strain by 43.8% in that zone, the largest reduction observed across both design variants, and also lowered stress and strain in the second, unmodified zone by 12.7% and 14.3%, respectively. Plate B reinforced both zones; this further reduced stress and strain at the second zone by approximately 30.6% and 33.3%, respectively, and reduced strain at the primary zone by approximately 40.6% relative to baseline. Relative to Plate A, Plate B showed a slightly higher stress at the first zone; this stress remained well below the original baseline value. This work shows that patient-specific implant geometry can be shaped directly by biomechanical feedback. This algorithm offers an efficient computational workflow, enabling implants that are not only anatomically tailored but also mechanically optimized as per given loading conditions.
